title: `<template for>` replacement in other then the HTML Namespace (SVG, MathML)
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Doing  `<Template for>` replacement inside an SVG or MathML Name results in a blank area instead of showing the content. This is because the template content is parsed as HTML part of the HTML namespace, instead of SVG namespace or MathML namespace. The namespace parsing should be determined by the location of the replacement (process instructions) instead of defaulting to HTML.


The following SVG example shows a blank square instead of a tomato circle
``` HTML
<svg width="160" height="100" viewBox="0 0 160 100">
  <?start name="svg-slot">
   <text x="8" y="20" font-size="12">Loading…</text>
   <?end>
</svg>
<template for="svg-slot">
  <circle cx="80" cy="55" r="24" fill="tomato" stroke="white" stroke-width="2" />
</template>
```

The following MathML example shows a blank area instead fo 1 +1 = 2

``` HTML

<math display="block">
  <?start name="math-slot">
     <mtext>Loading…</mtext>
  <?end>
</math>
<template for="math-slot">

<?start name="math-slot">
  <msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup>
  <mo>+</mo>
  <msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup>
  <mo>=</mo>
  <msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup>
<?end>
</template>
```
Here is a live [example demo](https://fast-page-ten.vercel.app/streaming.html)


This is a challenge for  `<Template for>` adoption in the framework space because users of frameworks assume that they can do any replacement with HTML/MathML/SVG/etc. Instead of just HTML, most/all current replacement solutions support this type of replacement.
